events.label: August 2022: the confession and its aftermath.
events.description: She tells her partner at the kitchen table. He is less angry about the money than about the months of lying. Their partnership, already thin, lasts another year. What she believes changes: she no longer thinks understanding a mechanism protects her, and she stops trusting her own calm.
events.region: Faye's kitchen table, north Swindon

events.label: Summer 2022: two months of hiding the loss.
events.description: She keeps checking a dead balance at night, tells her partner the savings are "tied up", and stops sleeping. What changes first is her body: weight loss, a tremor in the hand that holds the phone.
events.region: Faye's spare room, north Swindon

events.label: Writing this novel, autumn 2025 to autumn 2026.
events.description: Faye writes in the evenings after guiding at the stones, at the kitchen table in north Swindon. She is four years from her own fall and far enough to laugh at parts of it.
events.region: Faye's kitchen table, north Swindon

events.label: September 2025: Faye finds a trading app on her fifteen-year-old daughter's phone.
events.description: At the kitchen table her daughter shows her, half proud and half defiant, a small balance in a coin that a video told her about. Faye recognises the feeling in her own chest before she recognises the coin. She has to choose what to do.
events.region: Faye's kitchen table, north Swindon

events.label: 2004-2008: the payments office as a field site.
events.description: She treats the office as fieldwork to make the loss bearable: notes on the tea round, the smokers' door, the appraisal. The notes are never written up, but the habit of seeing people as a band stays for life and becomes her way of writing.
events.region: The building society payments office, west Swindon

events.description: Instead of forbidding it, Faye asks her daughter to show her how it works. Her daughter keeps a small balance and starts asking better questions. Faye starts the novel the same autumn, writing as someone walking bes…

events.label: Childhood in a railway-works family in north Swindon, 1979-1990.
events.description: Faye grows up in a terraced house in north Swindon. Her father has worked in the railway works since he was sixteen; the works hooter, the shift and the Friday pay packet are the calendar of the house. Her mother is a school dinner lady. On Sundays they walk on the downs, where her father shows her the chalk horse and says it has been kept white for three t…
events.region: Swindon, Wiltshire, England

events.label: Secondary school and the sixth form, 1990-1997.
events.description: A clever, watchful teenager who reads archaeology books from the town library and works Saturdays at a supermarket checkout. Her father drinks more; her mother holds the house together. A history teacher takes her class to Avebury and she stays behind in the rain to count the stones.
events.region: Swindon, Wiltshire, England

events.label: Archaeology, then a doctorate on Neolithic gathering enclosures, 1997-2004.
events.description: First in her family at university. She falls for deep time: the forager hundreds of thousands of years, then the first farmers who met at ditched hilltop enclosures to feast, trade and bury. Her doctorate asks why scattered herders began gathering in one place at set seasons: the beginning of institutions.
events.region: A university town on the English south coast

events.label: Eighteen years in a building society payments operations team, 2004-2022.
events.description: She learns the batch: payment files that run overnight, exceptions that must be cleared before the cut-off, a three-day cycle designed in the 1960s. She becomes the person who knows why a payment failed. She meets her partner, a secondary-school geography teacher, in 2008; their daughter is born in 2011.
events.region: The building society payments office, west Swindon

events.label: The decentralized-finance rabbit hole, 2020-2022.
events.description: Working from home in the 2020 lockdown, she follows a younger colleague into decentralized finance. She understands the mechanisms quickly and loves it: money as open code, a ledger anyone can read. She moves most of the family savings in, grows them, joins a chat server where people talk through the night, and holds through the spring 2022 collapse.
events.region: Faye's spare room in north Swindon, and online

events.label: After: separation, the stones and the novel, 2022-2026.
events.description: She confesses the loss in summer 2022; she and her partner separate in 2023 and share the care of their daughter. After redundancy she becomes a seasonal guide at the Avebury stones and writes fiction in the evenings, finishing this novel in 2026 when her daughter is fifteen and has a trading app on her phone.
events.region: Avebury and the Marlborough Downs, Wiltshire

events.label: 2023-2025: guiding at the stones.
events.description: She learns to talk to strangers for a living, which she had never done. Visitors ask why anyone would drag a forty-ton stone across the downs; she finds herself answering that people will do almost anything to gather. She begins writing fiction in the evenings in 2024.
events.region: Avebury and the Marlborough Downs, Wiltshire
